description: Combined PRD evidence from two isolated Codex/Ralph stream worktrees. Verification and PR gate run on this integration branch.

userStories.title: Reject malformed stream ingest edits before publish
userStories.problem: The stream ingest API validates request size and metadata, but malformed edit envelopes with an empty or unknown edit type, missing primary key, or incomplete link edit identity can still reach the publisher. That turns caller-visible success into delayed consumer failure or DLQ handling instead of a deterministic API rejection.
userStories.userStory: As an ontology data operator, I want stream ingest to fail fast on malformed edit envelopes so accepted ingest batches are well-formed before they enter the funnel.
bddAcceptance: Given a stream ingest request with an edit type outside CREATE, MODIFY, DELETE, LINK_CREATE, and LINK_DELETE, when the request is posted, then the API returns 400 InvalidEdit and does not publish a batch.
Given a stream ingest request with a CREATE, MODIFY, or DELETE edit missing primaryKey, when the request is posted, then the API returns 400 InvalidEdit and does not publish a batch.

Given a stream ingest request with a LINK_CREATE or LINK_DELETE edit missing linkTypeRid or targetPrimaryKey, when the request is posted, then the API returns 400 InvalidEdit and does not publish a batch.
Given a valid CREATE ingest edit, when the request is posted, then the existing source tagging, URL objectType coercion, and success response are preserved.

userStories.title: Support JSON-RPC batch envelopes in MCP transports
userStories.problem: The MCP server currently parses only a single JSON-RPC request per HTTP body or stdio line, so a standards-compliant JSON-RPC batch envelope is treated as an invalid single request.
userStories.userStory: As an MCP client, I want Weave to process JSON-RPC batch envelopes so multiple tool/resource calls can be sent efficiently while notifications still omit responses.
bddAcceptance: Given an HTTP MCP POST body containing a batch with initialize, tools/list, and a notification, when it is handled, then the response is a JSON array containing only the two request responses.
Given a stdio MCP line containing the same batch, when it is handled, then one output line contains the response array.
Given an empty JSON-RPC batch, when it is handled, then Weave returns a JSON-RPC InvalidRequest error.

userStories.title: Make MCP HTTP body-limit failures transport-level
userStories.problem: The MCP HTTP transport comments reserve non-200 responses for transport-level failures such as content too large, but oversized bodies are currently encoded as JSON-RPC InvalidRequest with HTTP 200.
userStories.userStory: As an MCP client, I want oversized HTTP requests to receive a transport-level rejection so I can distinguish protocol errors from request-size enforcement.
bddAcceptance: Given a POST /mcp request body larger than the configured limit, when it is handled, then the response status is 413 and no JSON-RPC success envelope is emitted.
Given valid JSON below the limit, when it is handled, then existing JSON-RPC status and response behavior remain unchanged.

userStories.title: Repair React 19 realtime subscription ref handling
userStories.asA: browser operator using live object and ObjectSet views
userStories.iWant: WebSocket and SSE subscription hooks to keep latest callbacks without mutating refs during render
userStories.soThat: realtime browser dogfood remains compatible with React 19 lint/compiler rules while preserving callback freshness across rerenders

acceptanceCriteria.given: a WebSocket subscription is mounted and then rerendered with a new onEvent callback without reconnecting
acceptanceCriteria.when: the existing socket receives an objectChanged frame
acceptanceCriteria.then: only the latest callback receives the event

acceptanceCriteria.given: an ObjectSet SSE subscription is mounted and then rerendered with a new onEvent callback without reconnecting
acceptanceCriteria.when: the existing EventSource receives a message
acceptanceCriteria.then: only the latest callback receives the event

acceptanceCriteria.given: React 19 hook lint rules are run against both realtime subscription hooks
acceptanceCriteria.then: it reports no react-hooks/refs render-time ref mutation errors

verification: cd web && npx eslint src/hooks/useWebSocketSubscription.ts src/hooks/useObjectSetSubscription.ts
